about: Scenarios (docs/ENGINEERING_SYSTEM.md section 3.2). State is derived from the proof each names; a scenario is never itself proof. PROTOCOL-class: changing this file needs an approval record.

scenarios.name: Orb asks for no network permission
mustNot: a network path off the phone

proof.check: the manifest asks for no INTERNET

scenarios.name: The fit report record is numbers only
given: a recorded fit report from a real-looking inbox
then: numbers, plus protocol and fit names
mustNot: a word of any message or any number of a person

proof.check: the record is numbers, plus the protocol and fit names
no word of any message, and no number of any person

scenarios.name: The fit probe prints counts and never a message
given: a backup whose messages carry a canary string and a phone number
then: counts and closed names only; byte-identical on a second run
mustNot: the canary or the number in any output

proof.check: the probe prints counts that add up and never a word of any message
the probe is deterministic: the same file gives byte-identical output

scenarios.name: The export analyser prints counts, field names and nothing a person wrote
given: an export with a secret planted in a payload
then: the chain, builds and counts; no payload value

proof.check: the command line: summary exits 0, a broken chain exits 1, an unreadable file exits 2, and no payload value is printed
a clean chain verifies; a removed event, a swapped one and an edited payload are each caught
only the latest numeric report is shown, only its numbers, and only for types on the closed list

scenarios.name: A stale mutant list is not a clean one
given: a mutant list whose text no longer occurs in the source
when: the harness runs or verifies it
mustNot: a list that proves nothing reported as clean

proof.check: a list with a mutant that no longer applies is not clean, and --verify finds it without running the suite
